page: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading and a dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

This instance utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 937 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not feature a GPU or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with the Geekbench single-core score placing in the top 10% tier at 2299.0. Single-threaded operations like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong results. However, multi-core and memory read bandwidth benchmarks fall into the lower 25% tier, as seen in the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and cached memory read tests. Redis SET operations also perform in the bottom 25% tier.

Given its high-speed DDR5 memory and local NVMe SSD storage, the i7i.xlarge offers qualitative resource density for storage-intensive and database workloads. It is well-suited for relational databases, NoSQL databases, and transactional processing where high local storage performance is required, though its lower multi-core scaling suggests it is less optimal for highly parallelized compute-heavy tasks.
